title: Atlas of lysosomal aging reveals a metabolite signature shared with lysosomal storage disorders.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Dryad API metadata and file listing: 48 files, 132.9 GB total; 47 are per-tissue/per-cohort zips of 0.6-9.8 GB each (metabolomics, lipidomics, proteomics of mouse, rat and macaque lysosomes), plus an 8.7 KB README.md. Tried to download the README; it returned 401 through the API and 403 through the public file stream. GEO GSE292311 summary: a bulk RNA-seq check comparing LysoTag and wild-type mice, young vs old, in 5 tissues, with only dozens of samples.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The abstract and Dryad description: lysosomal metabolite changes across tissues, linear increase with age, caloric-restriction effect, and a lysosomal 'aging clock'. Animals per group, the format of the zip contents (raw mass-spectrometry files vs processed tables) and the clock's method and accuracy were not retrievable: no full text in Europe PMC, PMC holds only the preprint abstract, and bioRxiv returned 429.

a1_downloadable.note: Dryad lists the files publicly, but the README could not be fetched programmatically (401/403). A browser download probably works. Not verified.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Age (young/old or age in months) is the natural label and is a sample attribute. Seen only in GEO sample titles, not in the metabolomics files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Unverified. The deposited zips are 0.6-9.8 GB each per tissue, a size consistent with raw mass-spectrometry runs rather than processed metabolite tables. A processed feature table was not seen anywhere.

a4_units_stated.note: Not checked: no processed table could be opened, so units and normalisation are unknown.

a5_enough_rows.note: The unit is one animal's lysosome prep per tissue. From the design of comparable studies and the GEO counts, this is likely tens of mice per tissue and a few hundred samples overall, far below ~1,500. The exact count was not seen.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 132.9 GB deposited; each tissue is a 0.6-9.8 GB zip
a6_fits_laptop.note: Every data file is over the 50 MB cap and likely needs raw mass-spec processing, which is forbidden by project rules and too heavy for a laptop.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Can't check: no sample counts were available from either the paper or the files.

a8_label_provenance.note: Chronological age of the animals is a recorded fact, not a model output.

backbone.name: none (no pretrained backbone for untargeted metabolomics intensity tables)
backbone.licence: Dryad datasets are CC0 by default (not confirmed in API response)

integration.partner_dataset: Tabula Muris Senis (mouse aging single-cell atlas)
integration.join_key: tissue + age; no per-molecule standard IDs verified
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do lysosomal metabolite clocks track tissue transcriptomic aging? But the join is only at the tissue/age level.

controls.positive_control: Glycerophosphodiester and cystine rise with age (named in abstract)
controls.external_validation: Rat and macaque cohorts in the same deposit

honest_claim_h3: Lysosomal metabolite levels from a few dozen mice per tissue, all from one lab, separate young from old animals. That is already shown by a single-metabolite trend.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use metabolite levels measured inside purified lysosomes to predict an animal's age, and test whether the predictor transfers between tissues and species.
plain_idea.train_on: One lysosome metabolite profile per animal per tissue (mouse, rat and macaque). The number of samples is unknown, likely a few hundred at most.
plain_idea.predict: The animal's chronological age, which is recorded at sacrifice.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Aging biologists would get a 'lysosomal clock'. But the paper says a few metabolites already rise linearly with age, so machine learning adds little.

ml_idea: An age-prediction clock from lysosomal metabolomics with cross-tissue and cross-species transfer. Blocked because only multi-GB, likely raw mass-spec zips are deposited, and the sample count is small.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: no processed table was available. Raw mass-spec reprocessing of more than 100 GB is out of scope.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the Dryad README.md (8.7 KB) in a browser to see whether any zip holds processed peak tables, and count the animals per tissue.

verdict_reason: The only deposit is 133 GB of per-tissue zips (0.6-9.8 GB each), likely raw mass-spec runs. No processed metabolite table could be found. The number of animals is likely tens per tissue, too few for machine learning, and the age signal is already captured by single metabolites.
